firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:37:| 2026-06-28 | **QSPI read throughput — the serial clock (GCLK = 2×QSCK) was the lever, not per-access overhead. At 200 MHz GCLK (MCC max → 100 MHz QSCK), XDMAC mem2mem reads hit 18.2 MB/s → ~225 ms for a 4 MB splash, ~3× faster than SD (~750 ms). Read integrity verified at volume. Splash → QSPI via XDMAC mem2mem is GO.** Bench (`qspi bench`, `flash/qspi_smoke.c`) at 50 MHz GCLK → 25 MHz QSCK showed ~5 MB/s and I wrongly concluded "overhead-bound, clock maxed." Greg caught the datasheet note **GCLK must = 2×QSCK** and raised GCLK 50→200 MHz; everything scaled ~linearly (DRV_SST26_Read 4.6→14.8, XDMAC mem2mem 4.9→18.2 MB/s; the raw libc `memcpy` path stays ~2.5 — it is just bad on this region, ignore it). Read path = **XDMAC channel 1 mem2mem from `QSPIMEM_ADDR` (0x60000000)** — ch0 is the ISC histogram DMA, and the PLIB only tracks ch0, so we program ch1's registers directly. Integrity confirmed by `qspi verify 1024 4`: 1 MiB × 4 passes via **both** the driver and XDMAC, **0 mismatches** at 100 MHz, with a position-dependent pattern (catches misaddressing, not just stuck bits). **Two dead ends ruled out:** (a) making the QSPI window **cacheable** in the MMU **hangs** — cache-linefill bursts aren't serviced by the SMM slave (back out; XDMAC bypasses the MMU so it's unaffected); (b) **continuous-read mode (CRM)** only trims the instruction byte on *non-sequential* access, so it does nothing for bulk sequential reads. SMM tops out ~36% of the 50 MB/s theoretical (re-frames per access); the only path to ~50 MB/s (~80 ms) is the QSPI's RX-triggered streaming read — deferred as a mini-project, not worth it over 225 ms. | The clock fix flipped the verdict: at 25 MHz QSCK QSPI-SMM (~5 MB/s, ~800 ms) was *worse* than SD's read; at 100 MHz QSCK (18.2 MB/s) it clearly wins. 100 MHz is within the SST26's 104 MHz rating and proved data-clean at volume, so no DLL/read-training needed at this rate. 200 MHz GCLK is an MCC clock-config change (lives in MCC config → survives regen). **Gotcha for any raw SMM read (memcpy/DMA, bypassing `DRV_SST26_Read`):** the read frame must be closed with `QSPI_CR.LASTXFER` + wait-CSRA or the next QSPI command hangs with CS still asserted — the driver does this internally; raw paths must call an equivalent (`qspi_end_smm_read()` in the bench). Splash framebuffer is in `.region_nocache` (strongly-ordered 0x20000000) but XDMAC writes bypass the MMU, so DMA→framebuffer is unaffected. | 
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:38:| 2026-06-28 | **Config/operator settings (backlight %, mode toggles, calibration) persist to the onboard QSPI NOR (`SST26VF064BA`, 8 MB / 64 Mbit SQI) via flash EEPROM-emulation — a small wear-leveled ring-log, NOT a filesystem. No board EEPROM exists, so QSPI is the only non-volatile small-state store.** Reserve ≥2× 4 KB sectors as a ping-pong region: a save appends a `{seq, settings_t, CRC}` record to the next free slot in the active sector (page-program, *no erase*); when full, write the latest record into the pre-erased partner sector then erase the full one. Boot picks the highest-`seq` record with a valid CRC; a partial trailing record (power lost mid-write) fails CRC and falls back to the prior good record → **power-fail safe by construction**, no torn settings. This supersedes the spec §4.6.2/§4.7 plan to keep all config in `/marvin/config.json` on the SD card: operator/UI prefs must persist and load **even with no SD card inserted** (the SD is removable, QSPI is always present). Session/recording config that travels with the data can stay on SD. **Splash, when/if it moves to QSPI, is stored as a raw pre-decoded framebuffer blob at a fixed offset — also no filesystem.** | NOR semantics drive the design: bits only clear 1→0 on program; setting a bit back to 1 requires erasing the whole 4 KB sector, so "update a value" = erase+rewrite 4 KB. FAT makes that worse (every file write also rewrites FAT/dir sectors → write amplification) and FatFs is *not* power-loss-atomic → a mid-write power cut can corrupt the FAT itself, not just the value. The ring-log avoids both: erases are rare (~one per N saves, N = slots/sector) and alternate across sectors, giving effectively unlimited endurance for human-driven settings against the part's ~100k cycles/sector; atomicity is the seq+CRC scan. littlefs (Harmony File System can back it) is the fallback **only** if settings grow into many named, workstation-mountable keys — overkill for a handful of scalars. **Raw-only splash:** the seed `splash.jpg` carries ~2 s of on-target JPEG decode, which dwarfs any bringup savings, so a JPEG-on-QSPI splash would be *slower* than today's SD path — only a raw blob streamed straight to the framebuffer (no decode, no FS mount, no FTL — NOR has none) realizes QSPI's sub-ms bringup vs. SD's ~350 ms `ACMD41` power-up handshake. |

A new boot loader task (`ui/loader.c`) mounts the card, reads `/<card>/ui/splash.jpg` into a static buffer, builds a runtime `leImage` (format JPEG) + sets it on the widget, then `UiManager_EnableBacklight()` (backlight control moved out of `video` into `ui_manager` — the UI owns the display; it was only in `video` for historical reasons), and reveals the dashboard + brings video up. **Per-screen pre-rendered persistent canvases** (revised within-session — see bring-up #1/#2): every screen is MGS-**persistent** (built once, never torn down) and owns its own canvas/Legato-layer/HW-layer — Dashboard 0/0/BASE (RGB565), Nav 1/1/OVR1 (RGB565), Splash 2/2/OVR2 (RGBA8888, full-screen, topmost). The splash is drawn over the dashboard on OVR2; the heavy Dashboard paints **behind** it and is revealed (hide OVR2) already complete. **Off-screen paint:** all screens are built pre-scheduler (no concurrency); the normal Legato render task paints them once the scheduler is up, and the loader simply pends on the public `leRenderer_IsIdle()` before lighting the panel (no scheduler hacking — see bring-up #4/#5 for the suspend/pump dead-end). RGB888 splash via the canvas's own 32bpp mode (the canvas framework sets the HW-layer color mode from `pixelBuffer.mode`); the RGB565↔8888 BASE-swap of the first cut is gone. Missing/oversized/no-card → the panel's solid fill is the fallback. Seed `data/ui/splash.jpg` (placeholder). JPEG over BMP/RAW: BMP isn't Legato-decodable (only RAW/JPEG/PNG), so it would mean a custom parser + bypassing the `leImageWidget` path and would prove nothing reusable; JPEG reuses Legato's enabled decoder and **is** the album-art pre-load path. Splash kept as an MGS shell (Greg's call) for base-view uniformity even though its only real content is the loaded image; the image widget is code-added since it's runtime data. firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:135:- **QSPI NOR (`SST26VF064BA`, 8 MB) storage tiering — driver bring-up DONE on hardware (2026-06-28), settings approach settled, splash + assets open.** QSPI PLIB + `DRV_SST26` (SQI) bring-up is **confirmed on hardware** via the `qspi` console smoke test (session log 2026-06-28): JEDEC `BF 26 43`, geometry 8 MiB (read 1×8388608, write page 256×32768, erase 4096×2048), and erase/page-program/read-back all verify clean. So these are now **answered**: the driver's `ResetFlash→EnableQuadIO→UnlockFlash` handles the global block-protection unlock automatically (erase/write work with no manual `ULBPR`), and `DRV_SST26_Tasks` pumping is a non-issue (no poll timeout). Settings → QSPI EEPROM-emulation is decided, and **read throughput is now characterized and integrity-verified** (2026-06-28 decision log + session log): GCLK=200 MHz → 100 MHz QSCK, **XDMAC mem2mem = 18.2 MB/s → ~225 ms for a 4 MB splash, ~3× faster than SD**; `qspi verify` clean at 1 MiB × 4 passes on both driver and XDMAC paths. So splash-on-QSPI is **viable and decided GO** via XDMAC ch1 mem2mem (cacheable-MMU and CRM ruled out; RX-triggered streaming → ~80 ms deferred as a mini-project). **Partition map is locked** (`flash/qspi_layout.h`, decision log 2026-06-28): splash `0x000000` (4 MiB) · assets `0x400000` (~3.98 MiB) · settings `0x7FC000` (16 KiB). **Both runtime consumers are built + confirmed on hardware (2026-06-28):** (1) the **settings ring-log** (`flash/settings.c`, EEPROM-emulation; backlight persists across power-cycle); (2) the **splash read** (`splash.c` reads `QSPI_SPLASH_OFFSET` via `DRV_SST26_Read` — **263 ms, splash shows with the SD card removed**). Host→QSPI **provisioning** is via u-boot `sf` over JTAG (`openocd/program-qspi.*` + `qspi_console.py`) — no SD card-swapping for assets. The splash read uses `DRV_SST26_Read` not XDMAC: at 263 ms it's already ~as fast as XDMAC (~225 ms), so XDMAC-for-splash isn't worth the ~40 ms. **Still open:** the **assets read-side** consumer (icons/fonts/album-art templates from `QSPI_ASSETS_OFFSET`) is unbuilt — the provisioning tool already writes that region. **at91bootstrap lives on NAND and does not touch the QSPI — we own the full 8 MB at the app level (QSPI splash is firmware-only, no bootstrap change).** NAND (`MX30LF4G28AD`, 512 MB) holds the app image (at91bootstrap copies it to DDR at boot); SD card stays for recordings/keyframes/results/bulk art. **Note:** the 200 MHz GCLK is an MCC clock-config change — verify it survives/needs-reapply on MCC regen, and re-run `qspi verify` after any QSPI MCC regen.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:137:  **Load-time estimate vs. SD (measured 2026-06-28):** SD does the 4 MB raw RGBA8888 splash (1280×800×4 = 4.1 MB) in **~300 ms bringup + ~450 ms read** (~9 MB/s effective). QSPI eliminates the bringup (~1–5 ms) and reads faster: SST26 in SQI quad gives ~45 MB/s at the 104 MHz part max (~90 ms), down to ~25 MB/s if the controller caps SCK near 50 MHz (~165 ms) — so **~90–165 ms read vs. SD's 450 ms (~3–5× on the read alone), ~95–170 ms total vs. ~750 ms (~4–7× end-to-end)**. Assumes DMA from the memory-mapped region (a CPU `memcpy` is slower per-access). Endgame for a static splash: if the LCDC can scan straight out of memory-mapped QSPI (XIP), the DDR copy is skipped and load time → ~0 (at the cost of holding the QSPI bus during scanout). RGB565 (2 MB) halves the read numbers. Confirm the actual SCK rate on hardware before trusting these.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:212:The splash now lives in QSPI NOR, not on the SD card — **confirmed booting with no SD inserted**, splash up in **263 ms** (`SPLASH: 4096000 B from QSPI in 263 ms`).
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:214:- **Read side (`ui/screens/splash/splash.c`):** `Splash_Load()` dropped the SD/FatFs path (`Storage_Mount` + `SYS_FS_*` + chunked file read) and now does `DRV_SST26_Open` → `DRV_SST26_Read(s_fb, 4,096,000, QSPI_SPLASH_OFFSET)` → `Close`, falling back to the opaque fill only on a flash error. This also removes the SD bring-up (~300 ms) from the splash path entirely — SD still mounts later for catalog/recordings. `DRV_SST26_Read` (CPU) not XDMAC: 263 ms is ~as fast as XDMAC (~225 ms) since the QSPI read dominates and the strongly-ordered framebuffer writes overlap, so XDMAC-for-splash is dropped (~40 ms, not worth it).
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:215:- **Provisioning (`openocd/program-qspi.{sh,cfg,md}`, `qspi_console.py`):** host→QSPI over JTAG, mirroring the NAND flow — stage an init-and-stop at91bootstrap (DDR up) + a u-boot SF flasher + the blob into DDR, then drive the u-boot console `sf probe`/`erase`/`write`/verify. `splash` / `assets` / `raw` targets (settings region guarded); `shell` mode stages u-boot only for interactive `sf` poking. The **committed NAND-flasher u-boot already has SF** (`sf probe` detects the SST26) — it's the default `UBOOT_BIN`, so no qspiflash build was needed. Bugs found + fixed on first run: u-boot parses args as **hex** (pass lengths in hex), `sf erase` needs **64 KiB-aligned** length for this part (`ERROR -22` otherwise), and the verify must key on `: OK` / absence of `!=` (terse u-boot output substring-matched `Erased`/`were the same` even on failure). Heartbeat dots added — the multi-MB erase/write is silent for ~10-25 s (expected, one-time).
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:216:- **Boot chain reminder:** the `NAND: ... Copy 0x100000 from 0x40000 to 0x23f00000` lines at boot are at91bootstrap loading the marvin **app** from NAND — normal, unrelated to the splash (which the `from QSPI` line proves comes from QSPI).
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:220:`flash/settings.{c,h}` implements the persistent operator/UI settings store over the `QSPI_SETTINGS_*` region (16 KiB / 4 sectors → 64 page-slots). Each record is a 256-byte page slot `{magic, seq, settings_t, crc32}` (CRC over magic..data). Boot scans all 64 slots and picks the highest-`seq` CRC-valid record (else compiled defaults); `Settings_Save()` appends to the next slot and erases a sector only when crossing into it — always ahead of the live record, so it's **power-fail safe** (a torn write fails CRC → previous record wins) and **wear-rotated** (~1 erase per 16 saves, alternating sectors). Bitwise CRC-32, static scratch buffers, bounded synchronous polling (safe pre-scheduler). Payload `settings_t` = `{version, backlight_pct, reserved0}`, extensible via `version`. `settings` console command: `dump`/`save`/`wipe`/`stress [n]`/`backlight <pct>` (applies live + persists). **`settings stress` PASS at 200 and 1000 saves** — wipes, saves N (recomputable values), then reloads from flash and verifies the highest-`seq` record matches the last write; confirms ring wrap + sector erase never clobber the live record. Note: `qspi` smoke/`verify` write the same region (CRC-fallback-to-defaults makes that non-fatal). **Wired into boot (confirmed on hardware — backlight survives power-cycle):** `enable_backlight()` lights the panel at `Settings_Get()->backlight_pct` (lazy-loads the ring; compiled default 50% if no record — the hardcoded `BACKLIGHT_DEFAULT_PCT` in `ui_manager` is removed), and the `backlight <pct>` console command applies live + persists. First QSPI consumer is live; splash-blob + DMA load is the remaining one.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:232:**Net:** splash → QSPI via XDMAC mem2mem (~225 ms vs SD ~750 ms) is viable and proven; settings → QSPI EEPROM-emulation unchanged. Both QSPI uses green. Next: build the two consumers (settings ring-log; raw splash blob + DMA load) and lay out the 8 MB partition map.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:244:Confirms: pins (PB19 SCK / PB20 CS / PB21–24 IO0–3), quad-mode entry, 8 MiB geometry, and — the usual SST26 trap — the driver's init (`ResetFlash→EnableQuadIO→UnlockFlash`) clears the power-on global block protection automatically, so erase/program work with no manual `ULBPR`. No `DRV_SST26_Tasks`-pumping timeout, so that open concern is moot. The smoke test writes only the **last** erase block (`0x7FF000`) to keep low offsets free for the splash/assets. **Stack added:** QSPI PLIB → `DRV_SST26` only — **no Memory Driver, no File System** (raw blobs + EEPROM-emulation talk to `DRV_SST26` directly). Next: push SCK toward 104 MHz + enable DMA, then build the two real consumers (raw splash blob read, EEPROM-emulation ring-log for settings). Detail + load-time estimate in the QSPI open-questions entry.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:248:MCC reconfigured PC18 from a plain GPIO (`AC69T88A_BACKLIGHT_EN`) to a **PWM output** (PWM channel 0: MCK/1024, left-aligned, CPRD=256). The old `AC69T88A_BACKLIGHT_EN_Set()` macro is gone, so `ui_manager`'s `enable_backlight()` was updated to drive the PWM instead. New `set_backlight(pct)` helper: reads the channel period at runtime and sets duty = period·pct/100 via `PWM_ChannelDutySet` (writes CDTY while stopped, the update reg once running — valid both at boot and at runtime); `enable_backlight()` sets the default then `PWM_ChannelsStart`. Default **50%** (`BACKLIGHT_DEFAULT_PCT`); 50% = period/2 is polarity-independent. Duty is set before the channel starts, so it comes up straight at 50% with no transient. `PWM_Initialize()` already runs at initialization.c:443; the channel is stopped (no output) until `enable_backlight`, preserving "dark until splash". Confirmed working on hardware (50% at boot).
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:252:**Duty direction (SAM PWM gotcha):** SAM PWM `CDTY` is the time spent at the **`CPOL` level**, not absolute high-time. With `CPOL_LOW` (which we keep — it idles the pin low = dark when the channel is stopped, no pre-splash glare), `CDTY` is the *low* time, so raw `CDTY=0` = full bright and `CDTY=CPRD` = off — inverted from a typical "duty=on-time" PWM. `UiManager_SetBacklight` therefore sets `CDTY = period·(100−pct)/100`, so the API is intuitive (`backlight 0` = off, `backlight 100` = full bright; 50% is symmetric, which masked the initial wrong-direction bug). Can't get both idle-low *and* raw-`CDTY`-intuitive on this peripheral (both tied to `CPOL`) without output-override — not worth it; the software inversion is the clean layer. Confirmed on hardware.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:254:### 2026-06-27 — UI boot rewrite: splash module + ui_manager orchestrator, loader retired (confirmed on hardware)
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:258:**New module `screens/splash/splash.{c,h}` — self-contained, Legato-independent.** Owns its RGBA8888 framebuffer + canvas surface; `Splash_Load()` reads `/ui/splash.raw` straight into it (or fills opaque-black fallback), plus `Splash_InitSurface()` / `Splash_CanvasId()`. No layer choice, no Legato, no backlight — just "load my pixels."
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:260:**`ui_manager` rewritten as orchestrator + compositor.** Owns the canvas-id + HW-layer constants (single source of truth in `ui_manager.h`), a screen registry (`{init, get_root, host, canvas}` rows — Dashboard, Nav; add a screen = one row), the boot task, layer assignment, and the backlight. Public API shrank to `UiManager_Initialize()` (pre-scheduler: assign surfaces + create boot task) and `UiManager_SetSplashShownCallback()`. Boot task: **Phase 1** `Splash_Load` → bind splash canvas to OVR1 + backlight (Legato-independent, fast) → fire splash-shown callback; **Phase 2** (guarded) `init_screens()` (each `screenInit_*` builds into Legato layer 0, then detached so the next can) → host dashboard + nav → bind dashboard to BASE → paint behind splash → after `SPLASH_MIN_MS` hide splash and give the nav OVR1.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:262:**Layer assignment is now ui_manager policy, never screen-owned.** `bind_canvas(canvas, hw, mode, show)` is the one place a canvas meets a layer; it pokes the layer's RGBMODE to match the canvas (the XLCDC driver never writes it), so the old "restore OVR1→RGB565 for nav" special case is gone. Splash holds OVR1 during boot; nav is bound to OVR1 only at reveal (after the splash vacates it — never shared live). `screen_nav.c`: dropped the hardcoded `gfxcSetLayer(NAV_CANVAS, HW_OVR1)` and local `HW_OVR1`/`NAV_CANVAS` (now `CANVAS_NAV` from `ui_manager.h`); `Navigation_OnShow` is the layer-agnostic host hook. (Memory `marvin-canvas-layer-binding` strengthened — Greg corrected this repeatedly.)
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:264:**Services start at splash-shown, in parallel with screen painting.** `app.c` registers `app_on_splash_shown` (→ `App_StartServices()` + camera go-live; `VIDEO_WIN_*` moved here from loader), fired by the boot task the instant the splash is up, so everything's warm at reveal. `Loader_Start` dropped from `APP_Initialize`; `loader.{c,h}` deleted (− user.cmake), `splash.c` added.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:266:**Concurrency:** Phase 2 runs post-scheduler, so the root-list mutations (`leAddRootWidget`/`leRemoveRootWidget` — no Legato locking) are wrapped in `scene_edit_begin/end` which suspend `LEGATO_Tasks` + `SYS_INPUT_Tasks` (handles by name; NULL → unguarded + warn). Safe because at guard time no app roots are attached (splash is pure scanout), so Legato is idle (`Legato_Initialize` ran pre-scheduler at initialization.c:492, independent of the task). `GFX_CANVAS_Tasks` left running.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:268:**Confirmed on hardware:** splash comes up as before, dashboard reveals correctly, nav works — the rewrite is behavior-preserving. Boot-task stack is 2048 words (screens used to build on the SYS_Initialize stack); no overflow observed.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:279:Moved the splash framebuffer from OVR2 to OVR1 so the topmost overlay (OVR2) is free to draw an overlay over the splash later (e.g. a loading/progress bar). Reminder recorded: canvases don't own HW layers — bind at display time (see memory `marvin-canvas-layer-binding`).
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:281:- Splash and nav now both use **OVR1**, but never shown together (splash during boot → hidden at reveal; nav only opens post-reveal). The splash's OVR1 bind is sequenced **after** `screenShow_Navigation` so it's the binding OVR1 holds at boot; the nav reclaims OVR1 when first opened.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:282:- Color-mode handling: splash pokes OVR1 → RGBA8888 (the XLCDC driver never writes RGBMODE itself); `UiManager_RevealDashboard` pokes OVR1 back → RGB565 for the (RGB565) nav after hiding the splash.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:285:### 2026-06-27 — Boot-timing arc DONE: splash visible ~785 ms (was ~4.2–5 s)
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:287:Confirmed on hardware: image shows correctly via direct OVR2 scanout, `mount + read` **785 ms** (mount 330 + read 446 of 4 MB), and that's the whole splash cost — no separate paint window. Splash-visible ~5 s → **~0.8 s**.
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:290:1. **Splash-first reveal** — light the panel when the splash is ready, not after the dashboard paints (it paints behind, during the hold).
firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md:294:5. **RAW splash → direct framebuffer** — the ~1.77 s software JPEG decode (then a 1.46 s nocache double-blit via Legato) replaced by reading `splash.raw` straight into the OVR2 scanout buffer. Splash paint cost → ~0.

No dedicated conversion script — but the format is fully specified, so it's a one-liner. Here's what I found:

## What exists

- **`firmware/marvin/data/ui/splash.jpg`** (source) and **`splash.raw`** (4,096,000 B) — the raw is already in the tree, but there's no checked-in script that generates it.
- **`firmware/marvin/openocd/program-qspi.sh splash`** flashes the `.raw` to QSPI `0x000000`, but it expects an already-converted file.

## The format `splash.c` requires

Raw **RGBA8888, 1280×800, no header** = exactly 4,096,000 bytes (`program-qspi.md:110`). Any other size is rejected.

## To regenerate the `.raw`

ImageMagick one-liner:

```bash
magick firmware/marvin/data/ui/splash.jpg -resize 1280x800! -depth 8 RGBA:firmware/marvin/data/ui/splash.raw
```

Or with ffmpeg:

```bash
ffmpeg -i firmware/marvin/data/ui/splash.jpg -vf scale=1280:800 -f rawvideo -pix_fmt rgba firmware/marvin/data/ui/splash.raw
```

Verify the size is right:

```bash
test $(stat -f%z firmware/marvin/data/ui/splash.raw) -eq 4096000 && echo OK
```

```text
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Program a QSPI NOR region (splash / assets) from the host over JTAG — no SD card.
# Stages an init-and-stop at91bootstrap (brings up DDR) + a u-boot SF flasher + the
# blob into DDR over JTAG, starts u-boot, then erases + writes + verifies the QSPI
# from the DBGU console. macOS/OpenOCD only. See program-qspi.md. Mirrors
# program-nand.sh.
#
# Offsets come from default/src/flash/qspi_layout.h:
#   splash -> 0x000000 (4 MiB)   assets -> 0x400000 (~3.98 MiB)   settings 0x7FC000 (off-limits)
#
# PREREQUISITES (see program-qspi.md):
#   * JP4 (QSPI-CS) IN  — the part must be connected for `sf` to reach it. QSPI holds
#     no boot image, so RomBOOT skips it (won't boot).
#   * JP3 (NAND-CS) OUT and no bootable microSD — so nothing boots marvin and the
#     core is caught cold (DDR off). program-qspi.cfg refuses if the core is in DDR.
#   * Nothing else holding the FT4232H or the DBGU console node.
#
# Usage:
#   ./program-qspi.sh shell                    # stage u-boot only -> console (test `sf probe 0`)
#   ./program-qspi.sh splash [file]            # -> QSPI 0x000000  (default $root/data/ui/splash.raw)
#   ./program-qspi.sh assets <file> [offset]   # -> QSPI 0x400000 + offset
#   ./program-qspi.sh raw <qspi_off> <file>    # -> QSPI <qspi_off> (escape hatch)
#
# Env overrides:
#   BOOTSTRAP_ELF  init-and-stop at91bootstrap ELF (default: ../binaries/sam9x7-boot-none-4.0.13.elf)
#   UBOOT_BIN      u-boot raw binary with SF support, links/enters at 0x23f00000.
#                  Default is the NAND flasher — its build includes `sf` (confirmed
#                  `sf probe` detects the SST26), so it doubles as the QSPI flasher;
#                  no separate qspiflash build is needed.
#   FTDI_SERIAL    target a specific board by its FT4232H serial
#   CONSOLE        DBGU console node (FT4232H channel C); auto-detected if unset
set -euo pipefail

here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
root="$(cd "$here/.." && pwd)"

# QSPI region bases (keep in sync with default/src/flash/qspi_layout.h).
QSPI_SPLASH_OFFSET=0x000000
QSPI_ASSETS_OFFSET=0x400000
QSPI_SETTINGS_OFFSET=0x7FC000     # off-limits to this tool
=== splash.h dims ===
```
</details></tool-use>

7	/* Boot splash — a full-screen raw RGBA8888 image, NOT a Legato screen.
8	 *
9	 * It owns its canvas surface and pixel buffer and knows how to load itself: the
10	 * image lives in QSPI NOR (flash/qspi_layout.h QSPI_SPLASH_OFFSET, provisioned
11	 * with openocd/program-qspi.sh) as raw RGBA8888 pixels in the layer's native byte
12	 * order, so displaying it is a flash read straight into the canvas buffer (the
13	 * buffer the LCDC scans out) — no JPEG decode, no widgets, no Legato, no SD. Raw
14	 * over JPEG: a software full-screen JPEG decode cost ~1.5 s; raw trades ~4 MB of
15	 * flash for skipping it. Reading from QSPI instead of the SD card also drops the
16	 * SD bring-up out of the splash path — splash up in ~260 ms, no card needed.
17	 *
18	 * This module does the load only. ui_manager (the compositor) decides which
19	 * hardware layer the splash canvas is shown on and lights the backlight. */
20	
21	/* Assign the splash canvas pixel buffer. Call once pre-scheduler, before the
22	 * canvas state machine runs. */
23	void Splash_InitSurface(void);
24	
25	/* Read the splash image from QSPI NOR into the splash canvas buffer. Returns true
26	 * if it loaded; on a flash error the buffer is filled with an opaque fallback
27	 * colour and false is returned — either way the canvas is displayable. Uses the
28	 * SST26 driver; call from a task once the scheduler is running. */
29	bool Splash_Load(void);
30	
31	/* The splash canvas id, so the compositor can bind it to a hardware layer. */
32	uint32_t Splash_CanvasId(void);

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="Write"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Convert an image to the raw boot-splash framebuffer marvin expects.
#
# Output is headerless raw RGBA8888, 1280x800, in the XLCDC layer's native byte
# order: each pixel is the little-endian word 0xRRGGBBAA, i.e. memory bytes
# [A, B, G, R] (see default/src/ui/screens/splash/splash.{c,h}). splash.c reads it
# straight into the scanout buffer and rejects any size other than 4,096,000 bytes.
#
# Provision the result to QSPI with: ../../openocd/program-qspi.sh splash
#
# Uses uv + Pillow (no ImageMagick/ffmpeg needed). Any Pillow-readable input
# (jpg/png/...) works; it is resized to 1280x800 (aspect not preserved).
#
# Usage:
#   ./make-splash.sh [input] [output]
#     input   source image   (default: splash.jpg, next to this script)
#     output  raw blob        (default: splash.raw, next to this script)
set -euo pipefail

here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
in="${1:-$here/splash.jpg}"
out="${2:-$here/splash.raw}"

[ -f "$in" ] || { echo "make-splash: input not found: $in" >&2; exit 1; }

export UV_CACHE_DIR="${UV_CACHE_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/uv-cache}"

uv run --with pillow python - "$in" "$out" <<'PY'
import sys
from PIL import Image

W, H = 1280, 800
EXPECT = W * H * 4
src, dst = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]

im = Image.open(src).convert("RGBA").resize((W, H))
r, g, b, a = im.split()
# XLCDC RGBA_8888 word is 0xRRGGBBAA; little-endian memory order is [A, B, G, R].
data = Image.merge("RGBA", (a, b, g, r)).tobytes()

if len(data) != EXPECT:
    sys.exit("make-splash: produced %d bytes, expected %d" % (len(data), EXPECT))

with open(dst, "wb") as f:
    f.write(data)
print("make-splash: wrote %s (%d bytes, %dx%d RGBA8888)" % (dst, len(data), W, H))
PY

```

## `firmware/marvin/data/ui/make-splash.sh`

A bash wrapper around `uv` + Pillow (no ImageMagick/ffmpeg — those aren't installed):

```bash
./make-splash.sh [input] [output]   # defaults: splash.jpg -> splash.raw
```

Key correctness detail I verified rather than assumed: the output isn't Pillow's default `R,G,B,A` byte order. The XLCDC `RGBA_8888` pixel is the little-endian word `0xRRGGBBAA`, so per-pixel **memory** bytes are `[A,B,G,R]`. I confirmed this empirically against the committed `splash.raw` (first pixel matched to within JPEG-re-encode noise; the naive RGBA ordering was fully reversed). The script asserts the 4,096,000-byte size that `splash.c` requires and fails loudly otherwise.

I documented it in `data/README.md` (the file you had open), pointing at `program-qspi.sh splash` as the downstream flash step.

36	| 2026-06-28 | **QSPI 8 MiB partition map locked — `flash/qspi_layout.h` is the single source of truth.** Splash blob `0x000000` (4 MiB) · UI assets `0x400000` (~3.98 MiB) · Settings ring `0x7FC000` (16 KiB / 4 sectors). All boundaries 4 KiB sector-aligned; contiguous, no gaps/overlaps. Splash at offset 0 (raw pre-decoded framebuffer; 4 MiB holds full-panel RGBA8888 = 3.91 MiB, or an RGB565 splash uses ~1.95 MiB — the reservation keeps both open, format decided when the loader is built). Read-mostly bulk grows upward; the small, frequently-erased settings ring sits at the very top as a stable anchor, **wear-isolated** from the bulk. Settings get 4 sectors (2× the 2-sector ping-pong minimum) for ring headroom. UI assets indexed by **compile-time offsets** for now (flashed with firmware); a manifest sector / littlefs can be carved from the front of the assets region later if assets must update independently. | One header (`qspi_layout.h`) means consumers and the `qspi` dev tools share offsets — no drift. Settings-at-top isolates erase wear and gives a fixed anchor independent of how the bulk grows. **Dev-tool caveat:** `qspi` smoke (last sector `0x7FF000`) and `qspi verify` (top-down) write into the settings region — destructive to it, but the ring-log's CRC-fallback-to-defaults makes that non-fatal (settings just reinitialize). Run heavy `qspi verify` before the settings store is populated, or accept a settings reset. | 
37	| 2026-06-28 | **QSPI read throughput — the serial clock (GCLK = 2×QSCK) was the lever, not per-access overhead. At 200 MHz GCLK (MCC max → 100 MHz QSCK), XDMAC mem2mem reads hit 18.2 MB/s → ~225 ms for a 4 MB splash, ~3× faster than SD (~750 ms). Read integrity verified at volume. Splash → QSPI via XDMAC mem2mem is GO.** Bench (`qspi bench`, `flash/qspi_smoke.c`) at 50 MHz GCLK → 25 MHz QSCK showed ~5 MB/s and I wrongly concluded "overhead-bound, clock maxed." Greg caught the datasheet note **GCLK must = 2×QSCK** and raised GCLK 50→200 MHz; everything scaled ~linearly (DRV_SST26_Read 4.6→14.8, XDMAC mem2mem 4.9→18.2 MB/s; the raw libc `memcpy` path stays ~2.5 — it is just bad on this region, ignore it). Read path = **XDMAC channel 1 mem2mem from `QSPIMEM_ADDR` (0x60000000)** — ch0 is the ISC histogram DMA, and the PLIB only tracks ch0, so we program ch1's registers directly. Integrity confirmed by `qspi verify 1024 4`: 1 MiB × 4 passes via **both** the driver and XDMAC, **0 mismatches** at 100 MHz, with a position-dependent pattern (catches misaddressing, not just stuck bits). **Two dead ends ruled out:** (a) making the QSPI window **cacheable** in the MMU **hangs** — cache-linefill bursts aren't serviced by the SMM slave (back out; XDMAC bypasses the MMU so it's unaffected); (b) **continuous-read mode (CRM)** only trims the instruction byte on *non-sequential* access, so it does nothing for bulk sequential reads. SMM tops out ~36% of the 50 MB/s theoretical (re-frames per access); the only path to ~50 MB/s (~80 ms) is the QSPI's RX-triggered streaming read — deferred as a mini-project, not worth it over 225 ms. | The clock fix flipped the verdict: at 25 MHz QSCK QSPI-SMM (~5 MB/s, ~800 ms) was *worse* than SD's read; at 100 MHz QSCK (18.2 MB/s) it clearly wins. 100 MHz is within the SST26's 104 MHz rating and proved data-clean at volume, so no DLL/read-training needed at this rate. 200 MHz GCLK is an MCC clock-config change (lives in MCC config → survives regen). **Gotcha for any raw SMM read (memcpy/DMA, bypassing `DRV_SST26_Read`):** the read frame must be closed with `QSPI_CR.LASTXFER` + wait-CSRA or the next QSPI command hangs with CS still asserted — the driver does this internally; raw paths must call an equivalent (`qspi_end_smm_read()` in the bench). Splash framebuffer is in `.region_nocache` (strongly-ordered 0x20000000) but XDMAC writes bypass the MMU, so DMA→framebuffer is unaffected. | 
38	| 2026-06-28 | **Config/operator settings (backlight %, mode toggles, calibration) persist to the onboard QSPI NOR (`SST26VF064BA`, 8 MB / 64 Mbit SQI) via flash EEPROM-emulation — a small wear-leveled ring-log, NOT a filesystem. No board EEPROM exists, so QSPI is the only non-volatile small-state store.** Reserve ≥2× 4 KB sectors as a ping-pong region: a save appends a `{seq, settings_t, CRC}` record to the next free slot in the active sector (page-program, *no erase*); when full, write the latest record into the pre-erased partner sector then erase the full one. Boot picks the highest-`seq` record with a valid CRC; a partial trailing record (power lost mid-write) fails CRC and falls back to the prior good record → **power-fail safe by construction**, no torn settings. This supersedes the spec §4.6.2/§4.7 plan to keep all config in `/marvin/config.json` on the SD card: operator/UI prefs must persist and load **even with no SD card inserted** (the SD is removable, QSPI is always present). Session/recording config that travels with the data can stay on SD. **Splash, when/if it moves to QSPI, is stored as a raw pre-decoded framebuffer blob at a fixed offset — also no filesystem.** | NOR semantics drive the design: bits only clear 1→0 on program; setting a bit back to 1 requires erasing the whole 4 KB sector, so "update a value" = erase+rewrite 4 KB. FAT makes that worse (every file write also rewrites FAT/dir sectors → write amplification) and FatFs is *not* power-loss-atomic → a mid-write power cut can corrupt the FAT itself, not just the value. The ring-log avoids both: erases are rare (~one per N saves, N = slots/sector) and alternate across sectors, giving effectively unlimited endurance for human-driven settings against the part's ~100k cycles/sector; atomicity is the seq+CRC scan. littlefs (Harmony File System can back it) is the fallback **only** if settings grow into many named, workstation-mountable keys — overkill for a handful of scalars. **Raw-only splash:** the seed `splash.jpg` carries ~2 s of on-target JPEG decode, which dwarfs any bringup savings, so a JPEG-on-QSPI splash would be *slower* than today's SD path — only a raw blob streamed straight to the framebuffer (no decode, no FS mount, no FTL — NOR has none) realizes QSPI's sub-ms bringup vs. SD's ~350 ms `ACMD41` power-up handshake. |

214	- **Read side (`ui/screens/splash/splash.c`):** `Splash_Load()` dropped the SD/FatFs path (`Storage_Mount` + `SYS_FS_*` + chunked file read) and now does `DRV_SST26_Open` → `DRV_SST26_Read(s_fb, 4,096,000, QSPI_SPLASH_OFFSET)` → `Close`, falling back to the opaque fill only on a flash error.
